topPRs.title: ci: cap Rust build parallelism at nproc-1
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
Measurement branch for the `rust-build-release` OOM. Opened to get a timing number before deciding between this and bumping the resource class — see the thread.

## Why

`rust-build-release` is being OOM-killed. The kernel SIGKILLs a rustc process and cargo surfaces it as:

```
sccache: Compile terminated by signal 9
error: could not compile `example-exex-hello-world` (bin "example-exex-hello-world")
```

It is intermittent. Scanning every `rust-build-release` run back to 2026-09-10 20:22 (106 runs):

| date | success | failed |
|---|---|---|
| 09-10 | 7 | 0 |
| 09-11 | 60 | 0 |
| 09-13 | 4 | 0 |
| 09-14 | 21 | **5** |

First failure: [job 5566326](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5566326) on `sp1-bump-6.8.0` at 16:53.

**The resource class was not reduced.** `rust-build-binary` has been `xlarge.gen2` (8 vCPU / 16 GiB) since [#20917](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20917) in May, which was an explicitly same-size Gen1→Gen2 migration. The recent `ci: rightsize …` commits touched `rust-ci-cargo-hack` ([#22860](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22860)), `go-tests-with-fault-proof-deps` ([#22867](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22867)) and `op-acceptance-tests` ([#22859](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22859)), not this job.

What grew is demand. The build is `mold -run cargo build --profile release --workspace` with no `-j` cap, so cargo runs one unit per core (8) under `lto = "thin"`, and peak RSS is set by how many large binaries link at once. Comparing build logs across [#22791](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22791) (`kona-zkvm-canary`, merged 09-11 22:15):

- Pre-canary, [job 5563887](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5563887) (success): the last units are `example-exex-hello-world`, `op-reth`, `op-reth-sdm-fixture`; `kona-sp1-proposer` and `kona-sp1-super-range-executor` finished ~30 units earlier.
- Post-canary, [job 5567979](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5567979) (OOM): the last six are `kona-zkvm-canary`, `kona-sp1-proposer`, `example-exex-hello-world`, `op-reth`, `op-reth-sdm-fixture`, `kona-sp1-super-range-executor` — both sp1-sdk binaries now link alongside `op-reth`.

Cargo's scheduling is nondeterministic and that is one sample each, so treat it as the best-supported explanation rather than a proof. It fits the failure shape: ~20% of runs, not all of them, which is what sitting just over a memory ceiling looks like.

## Change

Export `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(nproc) - 1` in the `rust-build` command. `nproc` reflects the resource class on these executors — the `go-tests` job comment at `.circleci/continue/main.yml` relies on the same property — so this is 7 on `xlarge.gen2`.

This applies to every `rust-build-binary` job, both the debug `rust-build` and `rust-build-release`, so the timing cost shows up in both.

## Verification

- `bash .circleci/scripts/merge-configs.sh` → merges clean, 4859 lines; the snippet lands intact in `commands.rust-build` and the merged YAML parses.
- I could not run `circleci config validate --org-slug gh/ethereum-optimism`; that needs a `CIRCLECI_CLI_TOKEN` to resolve the private `ethereum-optimism/circleci-utils` orb, which I do not have. Orb resolution is therefore unverified — but this change adds only shell lines inside an existing `run.command`, and touches no job, executor, orb, anchor or parameter.

Baseline for the comparison, from the 40 most recent successful `rust-build-release` jobs: median 21.5 min, mean 21.5, range 18.4–25.7.

Prompted by: @wwared
